items.title: My Morning Jacket & Modest Mouse Share Their Covers From New Neil Young Tribute Albums
items.summary:
Modest Mouse and My Morning Jacket have released their contributions to the next two volumes of the Heart Of Gold series, the ongoing set of Neil Young tribute records. Both covers come from albums arriving November 6: Heart Of Gold: The Songs Of Neil Young, Vol. 2 – Out Of The Blue and Vol. 3 – Into The Black, which follow last year's first installment.

Modest Mouse teamed with the Chicago band Califone on "Barstool Blues," a track Young cut in 1975 for his seventh album, Zuma. It appears on Vol. 3 – Into The Black. Isaac Brock explained in a press release that he had started on a different song entirely: "I had initially chosen and started working on a cover of Cortez The Killer before I realized that, in order to pull this off the way I'd like to, it was going to take me a thousand hours."

Brock said he landed on "Barstool Blues" because he felt closer to it. "On top of being such a catchy song, it was something that I felt more of a mental and emotional connection to than 'Cortez' anyway, which I have more of a 'historical' emotional connection to," he said, adding that the hardest part of covering a song you know well is finding a version that isn't simply the original again. He also called the assignment "a stressful honor."

My Morning Jacket took "Like A Hurricane," written in 1975 and first issued on Young's 1977 album American Stars 'N Bars. The band recorded it live at Marigny Studios in New Orleans with the Preservation Hall Jazz Band and producer Ross Hogarth.

As Stereogum reported, the two covers join previously released tracks from the series, including King Princess on "Helpless" and Jaco Rosa on "After The Gold Rush." Proceeds from the albums go to The Bridge School, the nonprofit Neil and Pegi Young founded to serve people with severe speech and physical impairments. Both volumes are out November 6 and open for pre-order now.

items.title: Kendrick Lamar Joins Jhené Aiko on New Song “So Good”
items.summary:
Jhené Aiko has released Westside Whimsy, her first album in six years, and it arrives with a Kendrick Lamar verse on the track "So Good." The song is out now alongside the rest of the record.

The collaboration goes back further than most listeners may remember. As Pitchfork noted, the two first worked together on Lamar's 2010 mixtape Overly Dedicated, before either had broken through commercially.

Lamar returned the favor in 2013, a year after Good Kid, M.A.A.D City, with a verse on "Stay Ready (What a Life)" from Aiko's debut EP, Sail Out. After that, their direct collaborations stopped, though Playboi Carti placed verses from both artists on "Backd00rs" from last year's Music.

Westside Whimsy also features Larry June, Ab-Soul and Tyga. The album is available now.

items.title: Venice Critics’ Week Awards: Tommaso Usberti’s ‘Before the War’ Crowned Best Film
items.summary:
The 41st Venice International Film Critics Week has handed its Grand Prize for Best Film to Before the War (Prima della guerra), the Italian feature directed by Tommaso Usberti. The section runs parallel to the Venice Film Festival and is organized by the Italian National Film Critics Union.

Set in Italy's Po Valley, Before the War follows Guido, a man just past 20 raised amid violence and racism, and his encounter with Sonia, a young Kosovar immigrant. The jury — French director Chloé Barreau, Hungarian producer Júlia Berkes and industry professional Caterina Mazzucato — praised its "intense and vibrant direction" and the way "provincial Italy becomes the stage for violent passions." The film also took the Luciano Sovena Award for Best Producer.

Elsewhere in the feature lineup, Shalini Adnani's family drama Our Share of Sand won the Audience Award, and The End of Times by Bibiana Rojas Gómez and Juan David Cárdenas Maldonado took the Mario Serandrei – Hotel Saturnia Award for Best Technical Contribution, cited for combining VHS archives with AI processing. Dong Jie's Zoom In, Zoom Out, about a game designer searching for a missing roommate across real and virtual spaces, received the Circolo del Cinema di Verona Award for the selection's most innovative film.

In the shorts competition, according to The Hollywood Reporter, Noemi Arfuso's E-I-E-I-O won the Critics Week Short Film Award for its portrait of two synthetic entities plotting human extinction. Paoli De Luca's Revolver won Best Director, Where the Tears Wait by Caterina Bertini and Blu Diego Fasoli earned a special mention, and Giulia Cosentino's Se mai le cose took both the Best Technical Contribution Award and the Centro Nazionale del Cortometraggio Award.

The Queer Lion Award, given since 2007 to the best film addressing LGBTQIA+ themes, went to London, the debut feature from Brazilian directors Victor Di Marco and Márcio Picoli. The film centers on a young disabled queer man working as an erotic performer and dominant in a fetish house who is pushed toward a medical exam that puts his sense of identity and independence in question.

items.title: ‘Practical Magic 2’ Sparks Near $5 Million In Previews On Thursday – Box Office Update
items.summary:
Practical Magic 2 opened its previews Thursday with $4.7 million from 3,200 locations, a stronger start than early estimates had suggested. Warner Bros. and Alcon's sequel reunites Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman, with Alcon financing half of the roughly $70 million net production.

The preview figure runs ahead of comparable titles. Deadline reported that Bullock's 2022 film The Lost City took $2.5 million in previews on its way to a $31 million three-day opening, while Ticket to Paradise managed $1.1 million in previews and a $16.5 million debut. Warner Bros. and MRC's Wuthering Heights did $3 million on its Thursday and opened to $32.8 million, which puts Practical Magic 2 on track for something in the $30 million to $35 million range.

Reviews have not been kind — the sequel sits at 36% on Rotten Tomatoes — but the 1998 original fared worse with critics at 29% and still opened at No. 1 with $13.1 million in October 1998, finishing with $46.7 million domestic and $94.4 million worldwide on a B- CinemaScore. The sequel opens in 77 international territories excluding China, where it is projected to take $18 million to $23 million. It also has premium large-format screens this weekend, including Dolby Cinema.

Neon's Hope, the alien invasion film written and directed by Na Hong-jin and starring Michael Fassbender and Alicia Vikander as aliens, opened Thursday to $1.1 million at 1,506 theaters, including $305,000 in previews. A five-day debut in the mid-single-digit millions is expected. The film grossed more than $36 million in South Korea and topped its home box office two weekends in a row.

Meanwhile, Spider-Man: Brand New Day, from Sony and Marvel Studios, closed its sixth week with $27 million and a running domestic total of $926.7 million. That leaves the Destin Daniel Cretton-directed film less than $10 million from passing Star Wars: The Force Awakens at $936.6 million to become the highest-grossing release ever in the domestic market, a threshold it should cross this weekend. Disney's documentary Oasis: Don't Look Back in Anger and Angel Studios' Runner also open.

items.title: Charli xcx Announces U.K. and Europe ‘Music, Fashion, Film’ Tour Dates, With Audrey Hobert Opening
items.summary:
Charli xcx has announced six U.K. and European dates for her Music, Fashion, Film tour, all scheduled for February 2027. The run covers Dublin, Glasgow, Manchester, London, Amsterdam and Paris, with Audrey Hobert, the singer behind "Sue Me" and "Bowling Alley," opening every show.

The overseas leg follows a North American run that is about to begin. Charli plays Philadelphia on Friday night, then two shows in Brooklyn, followed by Toronto, Boston, Washington D.C., Atlanta, San Diego, two nights in Los Angeles, Glendale and Las Vegas.

Ticket sign-ups are already open. Variety reported that presale registration runs through Sept. 15 on Charli's website, with artist presale tickets going on sale Sept. 16 at 11 a.m. BST/12 p.m. CET and general on-sale opening Sept. 18 at 9 a.m. BST/10 a.m. CET.

The tour supports Music, Fashion, Film, the album on which Charli set aside the autotune and dance production that defined her earlier work in favor of a rock-leaning sound. Variety's Jem Aswad described it as "a sonic palette cleanser to launch the post-Brat era in earnest," writing that the record leaves her "free to go basically anywhere she wants in her next chapter."
